newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African cabinet meets on proposed Syria arms sale.
newsitem.headline: S.African cabinet meets on proposed Syria arms sale.

text.p: The South African cabinet met on Wednesday to discuss the possible sale of weapons technology to Syria, which sparked a row between Pretoria and Washington, officials said.
The United States has threatened to cut off aid over the proposed deal in which South Africa would provide tank-gun aiming systems to Syria, which Washington regards as a state sponsor of terrorism.
The Pretoria cabinet has already given provisional approval for the sale, according to leaked cabinet minutes, pending the approval of Deputy President Thabo Mbeki.
One official said Mbeki and Defence Minister Joe Modise, along with several other ministers, would address a news conference after Wednesday's cabinet meeting at 3 p.m. (1300 GMT).
Officials said the arms deal was expected to come up at the meeting, but that a decision might be postponed pending further investigation by the deputy president.

South Africa says it is just one of the countries, along with three in Europe, which are bidding for the $650 million contract, and that a U.S. defence contractor is involved in at least one of those bids.

President Nelson Mandela, who is attending the cabinet meeting, has taken a defiant stand over the proposal, saying South Africa alone will decide on the matter and will not bow to pressure from outside.
U.S. Senate foreign relations committee chairman Jesse Helms has urged President Bill Clinton to halt U.S. aid to South Africa because of the proposed sale.
Washjington has threatened to cut off aid worth $110 million this year if the deal goes ahead.

South Africa's opposition National Party of former president F.W. de Klerk has urged the government to veto the deal, saying it goes against the government's own guidelines on not selling arms to troublespots and jeopardises relations with Washington. The previous white government had close military ties with Israel.
